title: Customer Purchase Analyzer
question: A retail company stores the number of items purchased by each customer during a promotional event. Find the customer who purchased the maximum number of items. If multiple customers have the same maximum, return the first occurrence.
explanation: Traverse the array once and keep track of the maximum purchase count.

title: Employee Attendance Tracker
question: An organization records the number of days employees were present during a month. Return the number of employees whose attendance is greater than or equal to a given required attendance value.
explanation: Traverse the attendance array and count employees meeting the required threshold.

title: Delivery Route Adjustment
question: A delivery company has recorded package counts for different delivery zones. Due to a system update, the package count of every zone must be shifted one position to the right. The last zone's count moves to the first position.
explanation: Move the last element to the first position and shift all other elements one position right.

title: Inventory Duplicate Check
question: An inventory system receives product IDs for a shipment. Determine whether any product ID appears more than once in the shipment.
explanation: Use a hash set to track product IDs already encountered.

title: Support Ticket Analyzer
question: A support center stores the category of every incoming ticket as a string. Find the first category character that appears only once in the category code.
explanation: Count every character first, then scan the string to find the first character with frequency one.

title: Employee ID Verification
question: An organization receives an employee ID string. Determine whether the ID reads the same from left to right and right to left. Return true if it is a valid palindrome ID.
explanation: Compare characters from both ends using two pointers.

title: Sales Frequency Report
question: A company wants to know how many times each product was sold during a day. Given product IDs, return the frequency of a specified product ID.
explanation: Store product frequencies in a hash map and retrieve the count for the requested product.

title: Customer Feedback Cleaner
question: A customer feedback system receives a text string. Remove all repeated spaces so that words are separated by exactly one space.
explanation: Process the string and add a space only when the previous character is not already a space.

title: Transaction Pair Finder
question: A banking application needs to identify two transactions whose amounts add up to a specified target amount. Return their indices.
explanation: Use a hash map to store previously processed transaction amounts and search for the required complement.

title: Employee Salary Search
question: An HR system stores employee salaries in sorted order. Given a salary, determine whether an employee with exactly that salary exists and return its index.
explanation: Because salaries are sorted, use binary search to repeatedly reduce the search range by half.

title: Product Code Lookup
question: A warehouse maintains sorted product codes. Given a product code, find its position using an efficient searching technique.
explanation: Use binary search because the product codes are sorted.

title: Monthly Sales Sorting
question: A company wants to arrange monthly sales figures from lowest to highest before generating a report. Sort the given sales values.
explanation: Sort the sales values in ascending order using an appropriate sorting algorithm.

title: Priority Task Ordering
question: A project management system stores task priorities where a smaller number represents a higher priority. Arrange all tasks from highest priority to lowest priority.
explanation: Compare and rearrange task priorities so that the smallest priority values appear first.

title: Search Optimization
question: A company searches for a customer ID in an unsorted list using a sequential search. Given N customer IDs, determine the worst-case time complexity of this search operation.
explanation: In the worst case, sequential search may inspect every element, so its time complexity is O(n).

title: Report Generation Complexity
question: A reporting program processes every employee once and performs a constant amount of work for each employee. Determine its time complexity for N employees.
explanation: The program performs constant work for each of N employees, resulting in linear time complexity O(n).

title: Duplicate Transaction Detector
question: A payment company receives transaction IDs. Determine whether any transaction ID appears more than once. The solution should be efficient for large input sizes.
explanation: Recognize the duplicate-detection pattern and use a hash set to achieve average O(n) time.

title: Peak Sales Period
question: A company records daily profit and loss values. Find the maximum total profit that can be obtained from any continuous period of days.
explanation: Recognize the maximum subarray pattern and use Kadane's algorithm to track the best continuous sum.

title: Customer Name Sorting
question: A customer service application stores customer names and needs them in alphabetical order for a report. Sort the names lexicographically.
explanation: Use a sorting algorithm to arrange strings in lexicographical order.

title: Efficient Product Search
question: A warehouse has N sorted product codes and needs to process many searches for requested codes. Identify the most suitable searching approach and implement it.
explanation: Since the product codes are sorted, binary search reduces the search space by half at every step.

title: Pattern Based Stock Analysis
question: A company records daily stock prices. Find the first day where the price is greater than the price on the previous day. Return its index, or -1 if no such day exists.
explanation: Compare adjacent values and identify the first position where the current price is greater than the previous price.

title: Memory Efficient Processing
question: A data processing application receives a very large array and must find the maximum value without creating another array of size N. Return the maximum value and use constant extra space.
explanation: Maintain only the current maximum value instead of creating an additional data structure. The extra space is O(1).
